Plot an ordination

Source: R/autoplot-ordination.R
autoplot.td_ordination.Rd

Draws a publication-quality ordination diagram in the style of CANOCO (ter Braak and Smilauer 2012): a biplot of sites and species for unconstrained methods and a triplot with environmental arrows for constrained ones, with equal axis scaling, zero lines and the variation explained by each axis in the axis titles. Species are drawn as arrows for linear methods (PCA, RDA, PCoA, db-RDA), whose scores are directions of increase, and as points for unimodal methods (CA, CCA, DCA) and NMDS, whose scores are optima.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'td_ordination'
autoplot(
  object,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  colour = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  sites = TRUE,
  site_labels = FALSE,
  species = 10,
  species_arrows = FALSE,
  arrows = TRUE,
  ellipse = c("none", "sd", "ci", "se"),
  level = 0.95,
  hull = FALSE,
  spider = FALSE,
  palette = "okabe_ito",
  theme = theme_tidydiversity(grid = "none"),
  surface = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  style = ord_style(),
  type = c("biplot", "gradient", "response", "scree", "shepard", "tvalue", "vandobben",
    "stability"),
  variable = NULL,
  axis = 1,
  model = c("glm", "gam"),
  layout = c("facet", "overlay"),
  n_axes = 10,
  nboot = 199,
  inset = c("none", "scree", "shepard"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A td_ordination from ord_fit().

axes

The two axes to plot.

colour, shape

Site variables (unquoted column names) to map to point colour and shape, such as colour = elevation. Sites are points, so they are drawn as categories (as in CANOCO), never on a continuous colour bar: a numeric variable with up to 8 distinct values gets one class per value, and otherwise is cut into up to 6 classes at pretty breaks; each class has its own colour and symbol. Discrete variables also define the groups for ellipses, hulls and spiders.

group

A site variable defining groups for ellipses, hulls and spiders, if different from colour.

sites

Draw the sites.

site_labels

Label the sites.

species

Number of species to draw and label, those best represented in the plotted plane (longest scores). Use Inf for all and 0 for none.

species_arrows

Draw species as arrows (a PCA/RDA biplot, as vegan::biplot.rda()), only for linear methods. By default species are taxa and are drawn as points (crosses) with italic labels, as in vegan::plot.rda(); arrows are kept for continuous explanatory variables.

arrows

Draw environmental arrows and factor centroids.

ellipse

"none" (the default), "sd", "ci" or "se".

level

Coverage of "ci" and "se" ellipses.

hull

Draw convex hulls around groups.

spider

Join each site to its group centroid.

palette

Colours for groups: "okabe_ito" or "grey"; continuous variables use the viridis scale.

theme

A ggplot2 theme, by default theme_tidydiversity().

surface

A numeric site variable to draw as a fitted surface: contour lines from a thin-plate GAM of the variable on the two axes (as in vegan::ordisurf()), or a linear trend surface (a plane, as vegan::envfit() assumes) with fewer than 15 sites, where a smooth surface would overfit. A continuous variable is a gradient, so it is drawn with lines (contours, or the arrows of the fitted formula), not by colouring the points.

size

A numeric site variable shown by symbol size (a bubble or attribute plot, as in CANOCO).

path

A numeric site variable, such as elevation or time: joins the sites in its order with a thin line and small arrowheads, so the reader sees at once how composition changes along the gradient.

style

Look of every element, from ord_style(): colours, symbols, sizes, line widths and fonts. The result is a ggplot, so any scale or theme can also be added afterwards.

type

The kind of diagram:

  • "biplot" (default): sites, species, fitted variables and groups;

  • "gradient": the ordination read as a gradient: sites (optionally joined in the order of path), fitted variables whose arrow width follows their r squared (non-significant ones thin, dashed and grey), the meaning of the first axis written at its ends, and the species sorted along the first axis in a panel below;

  • "response": species response curves: each species' abundance against an axis (axis) or a site variable (variable), fitted by a quadratic Poisson GLM (ter Braak's Gaussian response) or a GAM (model), with a confidence band from the model on the link scale, for the species best-fitted species, as panels or overlaid (layout);

  • "scree": variation explained by each axis, with the broken-stick expectation (n_axes axes);

  • "shepard": Shepard diagram of an NMDS with stress and R squared;

  • "tvalue": which species increase or decrease with one site variable (variable), the question of CANOCO's t-value biplot: species arrows coloured by an exact t-test of their coefficient in a regression of each (transformed) species on all site variables. Van Dobben circles are not drawn, as they only approximate these tests under one scaling.

  • "vandobben": CANOCO's t-value biplot with Van Dobben circles for one numeric site variable (variable): species and variables placed by a rank-2 approximation of the matrix of t-values of regression coefficients; the dashed circles mark, approximately, species with a significant positive (red) or negative (blue) coefficient, and the colours give the exact t-tests;

  • "stability": how robust each site's position is: 95% ellipses of nboot bootstrap ordinations (species resampled), rotated onto the original by Procrustes analysis (unconstrained methods).

variable, axis, model, layout, n_axes, nboot

Options of type (see above).

inset

For the biplot, a small diagnostic panel in a corner: "scree" (variance per axis) or "shepard" (NMDS fit).

...

Not used.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Groups of sites can be summarised with ellipses, convex hulls or spiders. Ellipses follow vegan::ordiellipse(): "sd" covers one standard deviation of the points, "ci" the region expected to hold level of the points, and "se" a level confidence region for the group centroid.

How to read the lines:

  • red arrows from the origin: species (linear methods only);

  • dark arrows from the origin: quantitative environmental variables;

  • dark triangles: centroids of factor levels (for example years);

  • coloured outlines: ellipses or convex hulls around groups of sites, and, with spider = TRUE, lines from each group centroid to its sites;

  • faint dotted grey lines: label leaders, joining a label that had to be moved to avoid overlap to its point. They carry no information.

Every option is an argument, and the result is an ordinary ggplot that can be changed further with +.

References

ter Braak, C. J. F. and Smilauer, P. (2012). Canoco reference manual and user's guide: software for ordination (version 5.0). Microcomputer Power, Ithaca, USA.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
data("dune", "dune.env", package = "vegan")
d <- community_long(cbind(site = rownames(dune), dune.env, dune),
  cols = dplyr::all_of(names(dune))
)

# RDA triplot of the dune meadows: A1 horizon as an arrow, management
# types as centroids with one-SD ellipses
ord <- ord_fit(d,
  abundance = abundance, method = "rda", transform = "hellinger",
  formula = ~ A1 + Management
)
autoplot(ord, colour = Management, ellipse = "sd")


# Which species respond to the A1 horizon? Van Dobben circles
autoplot(ord, type = "vandobben", variable = "A1")


# NMDS with the A1 horizon as contours and a Shepard inset
nmds <- ord_fit(d, abundance = abundance, method = "nmds", formula = ~A1)
autoplot(nmds, surface = A1, inset = "shepard")
